# Polymend

> Polymend (https://polymend.xyz) is a free, open-source mesh repair tool for 3D printing. It repairs STL and GLB files so a slicer accepts them. It runs entirely in the browser; files are never uploaded.

## What it does

- Fixes the mesh faults slicers report as open edges, non-manifold edges and reversed faces: it removes stray triangles stuck to the surface, patches small holes (up to 100 edges), and turns wrongly facing triangles.
- Converts GLB to STL or 3MF, turning the model upright and letting the user set a print height in millimeters.
- Shows the model before and after, side by side, with every change marked, and reports "Repaired", "Nothing to fix" or "Partly repaired".
- Leaves original vertices where they are. It does not fix large holes, self-intersections or badly damaged scans, and says so when faults remain.

## Facts

- Input: GLB (uncompressed binary glTF) and STL (binary or text), up to 400 MB or 4 million triangles.
- Output: binary STL, 3MF in millimeters, or a ZIP of both. Color and texture are not kept.
- Privacy: no upload, no analytics, no cookies; the page's Content-Security-Policy forbids network connections.
- Speed: a 300,000-triangle model is repaired in about a second.
- Evidence: twelve detailed figure models, each with 6 to 54 non-manifold edges and 16 to 114 open edges, were all repaired to zero and imported into Bambu Studio without a mesh warning. Other slicers have not been tested yet.
- Cost and license: free; MIT license; source at https://github.com/heyhaigh/polymend
- Made by Ryan Haigh (https://heyhaigh.ai).
